sections.overview: This small Neotropical emballonurid bat is the only living species in the genus Cormura and is also called Wagner’s sac-winged bat.
sections.identification: Adults are about 5 cm long and 9 g, with a light-brown to black back, paler underside and elongated scent sacs on the forearms.
sections.habitat: It is associated with humid, continuous forests and waterways, and has been recorded across Central America and northern and western South America.
sections.diet: It is an aerial insectivore, hunting flying insects in forest gaps, along edges and above the canopy.
sections.behavior: The species is generally solitary and forages through several forest height layers, from canopy to near ground level.
sections.reproduction: The available species accounts describe its roosting and echolocation but provide little direct information on breeding or litter size.
sections.ecology: Its activity within forest interiors and edges makes it one of the aerial insectivorous bats monitored in studies of Amazonian forest fragmentation.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports a global IUCN status of Least Concern; this broad category does not remove the importance of retaining humid forest habitat.

sources.title: Edge effects and vertical stratification of aerial insectivorous bats across Amazonian rainforest — PeerJ
